prerequisites: Knowledge of the most common numerical methods for solving linear systems.
A basic knowledge of fluid mechanics as taught in the Laurea Triennale course.

learning_outcomes.text: Understanding and proficiency in numerical methods commonly used in engineering and typical multidimensional problems of fluid dynamics.
Knowledge of finite differences and finite elements, and concepts of convergence and consistency.
Knowledge of methods for solving one-dimensional initial and boundary value problems.
Knowledge of methods for solving multidimensional elliptic, parabolic, and hyperbolic problems.
Knowledge of methods for solving boundary layer equations, Stokes equations, and Navier-Stokes equations.
Ability to analyze and numerically solve typical practical problems in fluid dynamics.
Ability to discretize and solve typical engineering problems numerically.
Ability to discretize and solve linear and nonlinear elliptic, parabolic, and hyperbolic equations.
Ability to discretize and solve steady and unsteady boundary layer equations, Stokes equations, and Navier-Stokes equations in simple geometries.
Ability to identify the most appropriate methods for solving analytical and numerical problems related to the context under consideration.
Ability to work in groups and expose topics related to the matter in question.
The ability to apply their knowledge to contexts different from those presented during the course and analyze in depth the subject using materials other than those proposed.

syllabus_topics: FINITE DIFFERENCES: Classification of numerical methods. Derivata of finite-difference formulas and their accuracy.
HIGH-LEVEL LANGUAGES: Structure and style of a computer program.

NUMERICAL SIMULATION OF LUMPED SYSTEMS: Initial values problems and their solution via multi-step and multi-stage methods. Zero and absolute stability. Modal analysis. Consistency, stability and convergence. Boundary value problems and their solution via shooting or direct methods.

NUMERICAL SOLUTION OF PROBLEMS DEPENDING ON SPACE AND TIME: Classification of PDEs. Methods for 1D heat equation and their stability. Semi-discretisation. Hyperbolic equations and the theory of characteristics. Equation of convection and its discretisation. CFL condition.

NUMERICAL SOLUTION OF SPATIAL PROBLEMS IN 2D AND 3D: Elliptic problems and their solution by direct (LU decomposition) and iterative (Jacobi, Gauss-Seidel, ADI) methods. Estimate of resolution time. Outlines of multigrid methods.
BOUNDARY LAYER EQUATIONS: Derivation via asymptotic expansion. Von Mises transform. Similarity solutions. Numerical solution in primitive variables and in stream function formulation.

STOKES EQUATIONS: Character of the equations and boundary conditions. Primitive variables and stream function - vorticity formulation. Colocated and staggered grids. Solution via direct and iterative methods. Pressure correction method.
NAVIER-STOKES EQUATIONS: Discretisation of convective terms: Stream function-vorticity and primitive variable formulations. Conservative discretisation and implications for numerical stability.
teaching_methods: Practice classes (implementation and testing of numerical algorithms, code development with student participation)
assessment_rules: The final grade will be out of thirty. The minimum grade (18 out of 30) is obtained through a correct modelling and a sufficient overall knowledge of the course topics. A grade of 30 out of 30 is proposed to students who show sound solutions from qualitative and quantitative points of view with thorough and deep knowledge of the course topics.
